How build-out is built

Every parcel carries its adopted land use and a unit demand factor from the agency's own meter data. Build-out is the sum. The growth case only phases that total in time, so build-out stays separate from the growth assumption. A new land use layer re-runs the sum; the unit factors change only in a master plan update.

Valley 16 in. loop

X11 | Distribution
expansion

Valley 16 in. loop is a distribution project in the Valley High area. Its purpose: fire flow deficiency, valley high. It is planned for 2029. About 8,176 customers benefit. New development pays for it through the connection charge. The planning-level cost is about $5.3 M in 2026 dollars.

What data would sharpen this

  • Break records tied to a main id. The flags here use a count per main that was matched by hand.
  • Installation dates on every main. Where the year is missing the main is assumed old.
  • Model results on each main at build-out, not only by zone, so the deficit flag is per main.
  • A physical condition assessment of the recommended mains before the design decision.

Valley 16 in. loop

X11 | Distribution
expansion

How unit costs are built

Each standard item takes one price from the agency's bids by a stated rule. Items roll up into assemblies, such as the cost per foot of a 12-inch main in a collector street with its trench, paving, valves and services. Each project is its quantity times its assembly, plus contingency by estimate class and the soft costs. A new bid changes every project that uses the items it priced.

How bid tabs become unit costs

Each bid is imported once. Every bid line is matched to a standard item, such as an 8-inch open-cut PVC main with concrete encasement, and the match is remembered for that bidder. Costs that are not per foot, such as mobilization, valves and design, are spread into the cost per foot of main. Prices are brought to the cost year, then combined across bids by a stated rule. The spread of prices is kept, so the reader can see how firm each unit cost is.

Import

Import a bid tab after each bid, or batch the year's bids at once. A new layout needs a one-time column setup, which the wizard saves per bidder.

Update

how the plan stays current: the annual checklist, the checks, and the record of every change

Annual update checklist Level 2 option

Work down the list once a year, or when a new bid or a new land use plan arrives. Each step says what to load, checks the file against its template, shows the changes it proposes, and records what it changed. Next update due 2027-10-01. Open the Tours button for a guided walk-through.

  1. 1
    Load the adopted land use export after the general plan changes. Land use layer
    A parcel export with adopted land use and development status. The build-out sum re-runs; the unit factors stay.
    Effect: re-runs the build-out demand by zone and moves the expansion triggers.

    Edit mode is off

  2. 2
    Add the year's maximum-day production from SCADA. This year's maximum day
    One row per year: date and maximum day in mgd. The tracker moves; the projection does not.
    Effect: updates the phase trigger tracker.

    Edit mode is off

  3. 3
    Import each bid tab through the wizard, after each bid or once a year. Bid tabs
    An Excel bid tab. The wizard matches each line to a standard item and saves the matches per bidder.
    Effect: updates the unit costs and re-prices every project that uses them.

    Edit mode is off

  4. 4
    Load the result tables from the latest model run. Model result tables
    WSC runs the model and sends the zone result tables. The screen shows the run date. No other screen changes the model results.
    Effect: replaces the model results and their run date.

    Edit mode is off

  5. 5
    Review the proposed changes and the act, watch or defer list on the Plan screen.
    A project that moved more than the threshold is flagged there.
  6. 6
    Save a snapshot and set the next due date.
    The snapshot fixes what this update changed. The due date drives the reminder on the Plan screen.

    Edit mode is off Set the due date

User guide

Getting started

What this file is

The master plan in one file that opens in any browser. It holds the build-out demand, the expansion triggers, the model results, the unit costs from the agency's bids, the CIP, a fact sheet for every project, the decision log and the map. Nothing is installed and nothing is fetched from the network. The basemap is built in.

The plan's data lives in a data file beside this page, never in the browser. The master file is shared on the network and opens read only. The editor password unlocks it for a session.

The screens

ScreenWhat it answers
PlanWhat needs a decision this year, the next expansion trigger, the CIP totals, what changed since the snapshot, and when the next update is due.
DemandBuild-out demand by zone, the expansion triggers against capacity, and the model results per planning year.
MapResults by parcel and by main. Click a facility or a main to see its recommended projects.
ProjectsThe CIP by fiscal year with the fund target, every project's record and fact sheet, the decision log, and the later-phase upsizing screen.
CostsUnit costs from the agency's bids, the assemblies, and every project re-priced. The bid tabs are the drill-down.
UpdateThe annual checklist, the checks, and the record of every change.

The top bar

  • Growth case, horizon and cost year sit on the screens that use them and apply everywhere.
  • Edit unlocks editing for this session after the editor password. Outside Edit mode every screen is read only.
  • How this is built shows the method cards: unit factors, the bid crosswalk, the assemblies and the markups.
  • Guide opens this guide at the section for the screen you are on. Tours lists the guided walk-throughs for that screen.
  • The gear opens Settings.
Tip. point at a figure, a column heading or a control to see what it means. On a phone, tap it.

Three things to know

  1. The plan adapts to new information. A new bid re-prices every project that uses the items it priced. A new land use layer re-runs build-out and moves the triggers. A year's maximum day moves the tracker.
  2. Model results are the one thing the file cannot recompute. They change only when the model is re-run and the result tables are loaded.
  3. Every change is logged with its date and author. Review each update for accuracy before relying on it.

Plan screen

Goal

Answer the questions a manager asks first, on one screen.

What is on it

  • Update reminder. The next annual update's due date. The banner turns amber 60 days before and red after. "Add to calendar" downloads a reminder for Outlook.
  • Data file. Which file you are working in, when it was last saved and by whom. The master is shared on the network; check the folder for a newer copy before relying on a figure.
  • Act, watch or defer. Every project placed by the thresholds under Settings. Act means the decision is due within the act threshold. Watch means it is due within the watch threshold, or the cost moved more than the cost threshold since the snapshot. Click a project to open its record.
  • Next expansion trigger. The next capacity step, its trigger demand, the trigger year and the decision date. The growth case moves it.
  • CIP totals. Five, ten and forty years, and the split between expansion and renewal.
  • Changes since the last snapshot. The latest entries in the change record.
  • Open decisions. Decisions in the log that still need a sign-off.
  • Figures at a glance. A tile from every screen; click one to open it.

How to use it

  1. Read the act list. Those projects need work this year.
  2. Check the next trigger against the latest maximum day.
  3. If the banner is amber or red, open the Update screen.

Demand screen

Goal

Show how much water the system needs at build-out, when each capacity step is needed, and what the model says about each planning year.

Build-out demand

Build-out is summed from parcels: each parcel carries its adopted land use and a unit demand factor from the agency's own meter data. The growth case only phases the total in time, so the ceiling does not change with the case. The chart compares the phased total with the adopted projection.

The horizon and the growth case come from the strip at the top of the screen.

Expansion triggers

A trigger is the maximum-day demand at which a capacity step is needed. The chart draws the projected maximum day with its band, the recorded maximum days from SCADA, and each cumulative capacity step. Where the projection crosses a step is the trigger year. The decision date is the trigger year less the lead time for design, permits and construction.

  • The alternative plant option switch shows how a different way of adding capacity moves the later steps.
  • The tracker shows how close the latest recorded maximum day is to the next trigger.
  • The maximum-day curve is the build-out demand times the peaking factor, so a land use update moves the triggers.

Model results

The table shows each zone's minimum pressure, fire flow, water age and storage for the chosen planning year, and whether it meets the criteria. The projects switched on in that run are listed.

Note. model results are read only. They change only when the model is re-run and its result tables are loaded on the Update screen. The run date is shown above the table.

Map screen

Goal

Confirm you are looking at the right asset and the right project before deciding anything.

What is on it

  • Color by draws parcels by zone, land use or demand, or mains by diameter.
  • Layers shows everything, hides the projects, or shows parcels only.
  • Pins mark every facility and every main a project touches. Click a pin to see the asset's record and its recommended projects on the right. Click a project to open its record on the Projects screen.

The basemap is built into the file, so the map works without a web service.

Note. this mock-up shows pictures of invented layers over a public basemap. The delivered file draws the agency's own layers on its own basemap, embedded in the file.

Projects screen

Goal

Hold every project once, with its reason, its cost, its timing and its stage, so the CIP, the fact sheets and the map all read the same record.

The CIP

  • List switches between expansion, renewal and replacement, or both. The horizon strip adds the later projects to the earlier ones.
  • Cost by fiscal year shows the next five years against the fund target. The dashed line is the cut line; years over it are named under the chart. In Edit mode, "set" changes the targets.
  • The table carries purpose, trigger, year, stage, zone, who pays, growth share, the connection charge id, the estimate class and the cost. Where a project was re-priced from the bids, the issued cost sits under the new one.
  • Click a row to open the project record: why it is in the plan, the trigger behind its timing, the area served, who pays, its assets, its decisions and its history.

Editing a project

  1. Turn on Edit mode in the top bar.
  2. Open the project record and choose "Edit project".
  3. Change the name, purpose, trigger, area served, planned year, who pays, growth share, assets, or enter a cost override. Leave the override blank to keep the re-priced cost.
  4. Save. The change is logged with your name, and the fact sheet, the map and the Plan screen show it at once.

"Change stage" moves the project through the workflow: draft, proposed, staff-approved, Board-adopted, deferred or complete.

Fact sheets

One page per project from the same record. The staff version carries every fact; the public version states the project in plain language and hides cost detail and asset ids. Print to PDF from the browser for the Board packet.

Decision log

Every assumption and approval with its date, basis and owner role. In Edit mode, "Add decision" records a new one and can tie it to a project.

Upsizing (later phase)

A desktop screen of renewal mains worth a larger pipe while the trench is open. Each candidate shows the in-kind cost, the upsized cost, the added cost and who pays it.

Costs screen

Goal

Price every project from the agency's own bids, in the cost year shown, with the spread of prices visible.

Unit costs

  • Policy is the rule that turns a set of bid prices into one unit cost. The default is the median of the three lowest bidders on each project, then the median across projects.
  • Standard item costs lists every item with its count of projects and bidders, the low, the chosen value, the high and the spread. Items with no bids yet use a reference price.
  • Cost build-up shows one project's direct cost, contingency, development and construction services.
  • Re-priced projects compares every project with its issued cost. A chip marks a move over 10 percent.

The cost year comes from the strip at the top. Prices from older bids are escalated to it by the index named in Settings.

Bid tabs

The loaded bid tabs and the prices per standard item. Import a bid tab after each bid, or batch the year's bids at once.

Importing a bid tab

The wizard has six steps.

  1. File. Choose the Excel or CSV bid tab.
  2. Columns. Confirm which column is the item number, description, unit, quantity and each bidder's price. A layout seen before is applied; a new one is saved per bidder when you accept.
  3. Match items. Each bid line gets a suggested standard item: a saved match for this bidder first, then the parser's suggestion from the size, material and unit. Change any match from the list, or exclude a line, or leave it for the review queue.
  4. Classify the rest. Lines that are not per unit of pipe are spread into the cost per foot of main. Mobilization, bonds and traffic control become a share of the measured subtotal. Valves, services, fittings and appurtenances become allowances per foot. Design and construction services become soft-cost percentages.
  5. Review. The prices per standard item escalated to the cost year, and the projects that will re-price.
  6. Accept. The tables update, the projects re-price, and the import is logged.
Tip. "How this is built" in the top bar shows the crosswalk table, the review queue and the saved matches.

Update screen

Goal

Keep the plan current with the exports the agency already produces, once a year or when a new bid or land use plan arrives, with every change checked and recorded.

The annual checklist

Work down the numbered steps. Each step says what to load, checks the file against its template, shows the changes it proposes, and records what it changed and who loaded it. A step that has run shows a green number and its last result.

StepWhat to loadWhat changes
Land use layerThe adopted land use export, after the general plan changesBuild-out demand by zone, and the expansion triggers
This year's maximum dayOne row from SCADA: date and maximum day in mgdThe phase trigger tracker
Bid tabsEach bid tab, through the wizardThe unit costs and every project that uses them
Project listThe finance project listProject timing and cost where a row matches
Model result tablesThe zone tables from the latest model run, sent by WSCThe model results and their run date

Then review the act, watch or defer list on the Plan screen, save a snapshot, and set the next due date.

Note. a file that fails a template check is listed with the rows that failed. Fix the export and load it again. Nothing is hidden.

QA/QC summary

The checks behind the figures: how many imports passed, the bid items still to review, the projects that moved more than 10 percent, the changes since the snapshot, the draft projects, and a self-check that the totals re-sum to the project list.

Change record

Every change in the file with its date, author, what it changed, and the value before and after. Export it as CSV for a review.

Snapshots and exports

A snapshot fixes the plan at a point with its stage. Export the data file, a dated HTML copy, or the next five fiscal years in the budget template columns.

Settings and files

Preferences

Theme, the default growth case and horizon, and whether the method cards show. These are kept on this computer and need no password.

Data files

The plan's data lives in a data file beside this page, not in the browser, so several staff can use the same plan.

  • Master file. The shared file on the network. It opens read only. The editor password unlocks it for a session. Choose it once; the tool remembers it on this computer.
  • Personal file. Your own file for scenarios and draft projects. Choose "personal" under "Working in" to use it. A scenario or project can be copied into the master with the editor password.
  • Before relying on a figure, check the network folder for a newer master. The Plan screen shows when the file was saved and by whom.

Other ways to control who edits the master, set up with the agency's IT at scoping:

  1. IT puts the master in a folder where only editors have write permission. No password is needed.
  2. A hosted version uses the agency's Microsoft sign-in and roles.

Plan settings

These need Edit mode.

  • Cost year defaults to the current year. Escalation index names the index used to bring older bid prices to it. Year of expenditure escalates each project to its planned year.
  • Act, watch or defer thresholds set the years and the cost change that place each project.
  • Steward, due date and fiscal year drive the reminder, the banner and the fiscal-year columns.
  • Editor password keeps casual edits out of the master. It is not security; the file is readable by anyone with the folder.

How data gets in

By delivery level

LevelHow a newer figure reaches the file
WSC-issued fileWSC loads the exports and reissues the file at each milestone. Staff read it.
Staff-updated fileStaff load exports on the Update screen. The file checks each one against its template and recomputes. Every change is logged.

By feed

FeedWhere it comes fromHow it gets inWhat changes when it is loaded
Land use and parcelsThe county parcel layer with adopted land use, exported from GISA GIS export loaded on the Update screen; or pulled from the feature service at the connected levelBuild-out demand by zone; the expansion triggers
Maximum dayThe SCADA historianOne row a year, typed or exported; or pulled from the historian at the connected levelThe phase trigger tracker
Bid tabsThe agency's bid tabulations in ExcelEach tab through the wizard; or a watched bid folder at the connected levelUnit costs; every project that uses the items priced
Project listThe finance project listAn export loaded on the Update screenProject timing and cost where a row matches
Model resultsThe hydraulic model, run by WSCThe zone result tables loaded on the Update screenThe model results and their run date
GIS layersThe agency's mains, facilities and parcelsRebuilt by WSC at each issue, or by the refresher at the connected levelThe map and the asset records
Decisions and project editsStaff, in Edit modeTyped into the toolThe decision log; the project records

What the file never does

  • It never connects to the model, the CMMS or SCADA on its own. Changes in those systems reach the file only when an export is loaded.
  • It never changes a model result. A different set of projects needs a model run.
  • It never changes a unit factor. New factors come with a master plan update.

Troubleshooting

What you seeWhat to do
A control is greyed with "Edit mode is off"Click it, or the Edit button in the top bar, and enter the editor password.
A control is greyed with "available from"The feature belongs to a higher delivery level than this file.
The banner says the update is overdueOpen the Update screen and work down the checklist. Set the next due date under Settings.
An import failed a template checkThe rows that failed are listed. Fix the export against the template named and load it again.
A project's cost does not match the issued costIt was re-priced from a newer bid. The issued cost sits under the new one; the change record says which import moved it.
The master file is read onlyThat is normal. The editor password unlocks it for a session.
Someone else saved the master after you opened itThe tool compares the saved time before it writes and shows the other author's changes. Reload or merge.
The file asks for the data file againThe browser forgot the file handle on this computer. Choose the same master file; nothing is lost.
The page shows a blank screen on a phoneThe iPhone Files preview runs no scripts. Open the file in Safari or a browser app.

Terms

Every term below also shows as a tip when you point at it in the tool.

TermMeaning
actThe decision on this project is due within the act threshold (Settings). Start the work that leads to the decision.
act watch deferEach project's recommendation. Act: the decision is due within the act threshold. Watch: due within the watch threshold, or the cost moved more than the cost threshold since the snapshot. Defer: beyond both. The thresholds are set under Settings.
added costThe cost of the larger pipe less the cost of replacing in kind.
alt optionAn alternative way to add capacity. Turning it on shows how it moves the timing of the next step.
annual updateThe yearly checklist on the Update screen: load the year's exports, review the proposed changes, save a snapshot.
assemblyThe cost per unit of a whole piece of work: a foot of main with its trench, paving, valves and services; a million gallons of tank; a million gallons a day of pumping or treatment.
average dayAnnual water demand divided by 365 days.
bid tabA bid tabulation: the unit prices every bidder offered on one project, line by line.
buildoutThe demand when every parcel is developed to its adopted land use. Summed from parcels and unit factors, not projected from a growth rate.
capacity stepOne phase of plant or facility capacity. Steps add up; the chart shows the cumulative capacity after each.
change recordEvery change in the file: when, who, what, from and to. It travels with the data file.
cipThe capital improvement program: every project with its purpose, trigger, cost, timing, area served and who pays.
cost buildupDirect cost, then contingency by estimate class, then project development and construction services, add up to the total.
cost yearThe dollar year every cost is shown in. Prices from older bids are escalated to it by the index named in Settings. It defaults to the current year.
crosswalkThe saved match between a bidder's description and a standard item. Reused on the next bid tab from that bidder.
decision dateThe trigger year less the lead time for design, permits and construction. The decision to proceed is needed by this year.
decision logThe dated record of planning decisions, their basis and the role that owns them.
deferThe decision on this project is beyond the watch threshold. Nothing is needed this year.
due dateWhen the next annual update is due. The banner turns amber 60 days before and red after. Add it to your calendar with the button.
edit modeUnlocks editing for this session after the editor password. Every edit is logged with your name.
estimate classHow firm the cost is. Class 5 is a planning-level estimate with a wide range; class 4 is narrower. The range is shown on the fact sheet.
fire flowWhether the zone delivers the required fire flow at the required residual pressure.
fiscal yearThe agency's budget year, set under Settings.
fund targetThe amount each fund can spend in a fiscal year. The cut line in the chart marks it; projects above it move or defer.
growth caseHow fast build-out is reached: low, base or high. Build-out itself does not change with the case.
growth shareThe share of a project's cost that serves growth and is charged to expansion.
guideThe user guide, opened at the section for this screen.
horizonHow far ahead the screen looks: 5, 10 or 40 years, or build-out. A longer horizon adds the later projects to the earlier ones.
how builtShows the method behind each screen: unit factors, the bid crosswalk, the assemblies and the markups.
in kindReplacement at the same size and material.
layersWhich layers the map draws. Pins mark facilities and the mains a project touches.
master fileThe shared data file on the network. It opens read only; the editor password unlocks it. A personal file holds your own scenarios.
maximum dayThe highest one-day demand in a year. Capacity is planned to it. Maximum day is average day times the peaking factor.
min pressureThe lowest pressure in the zone under the run's conditions, against the agency's service criterion.
model resultsFigures from the hydraulic model. They change only when the model is re-run and its result tables are loaded on the Update screen.
parcelOne lot in the county parcel layer, with its adopted land use and development status.
planning yearThe year a model run represents, with the projects switched on in that run.
policyThe rule that turns a set of bid prices into one unit cost, such as the median of the three lowest bidders.
qaqcThe checks behind the figures: template checks on every import, the bid items still to review, projects that moved more than 10 percent, and a self-check that the totals re-sum.
quantity effectA flag that a larger quantity won a lower unit price, so the price depends on the size of the job.
repricedA project cost recomputed from the current unit cost table, compared with the issued cost.
review queueBid lines that have no confirmed match yet. They do not price anything until matched.
snapshotA fixed point in the plan with its stage and date. Changes after it are listed on the Plan screen.
spreadThe low to high range of the prices behind a unit cost, with the chosen value marked.
stageWhere a project sits in the approval workflow: draft, proposed, staff-approved, Board-adopted, deferred or complete.
standard itemOne line of the standard cost list, such as an 8-inch open-cut PVC main with concrete encasement, per foot. Every bid line is matched to one.
stewardThe person who keeps the plan current and runs the annual update. Named at scoping.
toursGuided walk-throughs of the larger workflows on this screen. A tour runs on a throwaway copy and changes nothing.
trackerHow close the latest recorded maximum day is to the next trigger.
triggerThe maximum-day demand at which a capacity step is needed. The trigger year is the year the projected maximum day reaches it.
upsizingReplacing a main at a larger size while the trench is open, where build-out needs the capacity.
watchThis project is inside the watch threshold, or its cost moved more than the cost threshold since the snapshot. Check it at the next update.
water ageHow long water sits in the system before use. Long ages point to water quality risk.
who paysExpansion projects are paid by new development through the connection charge. Renewal and replacement is paid by existing customers. A split project carries a growth share.
year of expenditureA cost escalated from the cost year to the year the project is built.
zoneA pressure zone: the area served from one hydraulic grade.
Concept mock-up with invented data. Not an engineering deliverable. Every figure is illustrative. Staff updates are logged with date and author. Review each update for accuracy before relying on it.
